notes: PSA 4.5 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.07. Prostate volume 73 mL. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following a stable Gleason 3+3 biopsy result and rising PSA trend.

Recently retired bus driver with a history of prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosed two years ago. He has been under surveillance but now presents with a PSA of 4.5 ng/mL, up from 3.7 ng/mL in July 2024. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 19/35, primarily nocturia and weak stream. He is widowed but lives with his partner, and his nephew is his main next-of-kin. He cycles 20 km twice a week and consumes approximately 11 units of alcohol weekly. He had a surveillance colonoscopy recently which was normal. He is hard of hearing and prefers written summaries of discussions.

On DRE, the prostate is enlarged but symmetrically smooth with no discrete nodules or asymmetry, consistent with cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, BP 125/91 mmHg and HR 65 bpm. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable masses or organomegaly.

admin: Hard of hearing — speak clearly; prefers written summaries.
